title: Italian Wedding Soup with Acini di Pepe
description: Beef and pork meatballs, vegetables, tiny pasta and spinach.

items.note: not dried (1 slice rustic bread, ground in a food processor)

items.item: Low-sodium chicken broth or chicken bone broth (about 70 oz)
Dry acini di pepe or orzo

steps.do: Grind the bread into crumbs in a food processor. Chop the parsley, mince the oregano, and shred the Parmesan for the meatballs and for serving.

Combine the beef, pork, bread crumbs, parsley, oregano, Parmesan, egg, 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Toss gently with your hands until evenly mixed. Roll into 3/4 to 1 inch balls, small enough to fit a spoon and spread evenly.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Brown half the meatballs, turning to color 2 or 3 sides, about 4 minutes; two batches leave them room to brown. Drain on paper towels, keep the oil in the pan, and repeat. They finish cooking in the soup.
Chop the carrots, onion and celery, and mince the garlic. Roughly chop the spinach.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Sauté the carrots, onion and celery until soft, 6 to 8 minutes; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the broth, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Stir in the pasta and meatballs and lower the heat to medium-low.
uses: Low-sodium chicken broth or chicken bone broth (about 70 oz)
Dry acini di pepe or orzo

steps.do: Cover and simmer, stirring now and then, until the pasta is tender and the meatballs are cooked through, about 10 minutes. Stir in the spinach for the last 1 minute.
Serve hot, with Parmesan over each bowl.

items: Keeps up to 3 days refrigerated, airtight, or 3 months frozen. The pasta keeps absorbing broth as it sits, so thin leftovers with more broth.
Reader tip: cook the pasta separately and add it to each bowl if you want it to stay al dente.

Dried, shelf-stable crumbs throw off the meatballs' texture; fresh ones from a hearty loaf work best. Italian bread or sourdough (faintly tangy) both work; trim thick crust and measure the 1/2 cup, since slices vary.
No ground pork: use another 8 oz ground beef.
No celery: use 3/4 cup chopped fennel bulb or celery root, or leave it out and add 1/4 tsp celery seed with the garlic.
Acini di pepe is the first choice. Orzo, ditalini, pastina stars or macaroni also work. For a brothier soup, cut the pasta to 3/4 cup.
Kale, endive or escarole can replace the spinach. Add them with the pasta, since they need far longer than spinach.
Chicken bone broth makes a richer, fuller-bodied soup. Sodium varies by brand, so taste before salting. Leftovers may gel when chilled; they loosen on reheating.
For more depth, use homemade stock, simmer a Parmesan rind in the pot, or add fresh basil.
Homemade Acini di Pepe. Fresh beads cook faster than dried, so stir them in for the last 5 minutes.
Sartori SarVecchio, a Wisconsin Parmesan aged 20+ months, worked very well in place of Parmigiano Reggiano.

nutrition: Per serving: 396 cal · 29 g protein · 20 g fat · 6 g sat fat · 25 g carbs · 3 g fiber · 362 mg sodium · 4 g sugar
